cases.display_name: Advective clearance edge-condition case family
summary_lines: This governed reference case family anchors the experimental advective screening model at the two reviewer-critical clearance extremes: short residence time and long residence time under effective persistence.
It is intended to make weak-clearance versus strong-clearance behavior challengeable in a regulatory review context.
applicability_lines: Appropriate for claims about bounded concentration under effective persistence and directional sensitivity to residence-time assumptions.
Not a substitute for calibrated flow, routing, or site-specific hydrology.

source_references.title: ECHA EUSES support page
EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

review_notes: This case family is screening-oriented and should be used to stress-test the loss term, not to imply hydrodynamic realism.

cases.display_name: Advective duration plateau case family
summary_lines: This governed reference case family anchors long-duration finite screening behavior where the combined degradation-plus-clearance term drives the solution toward a duration-limited plateau.
It supports reviewer-facing discussion of why extending duration at a fixed release rate yields diminishing concentration change.
applicability_lines: Appropriate for finite-duration plateau reasoning within deterministic screening math.
Not a claim of infinite-time equilibrium, spatial dispersion, or field-scale hydrodynamic realism.

source_references.title: ECHA Guidance on Information Requirements and Chemical Safety Assessment
EPA Guidance on the Development, Evaluation, and Application of Environmental Models

review_notes: Use this case family when the reviewer needs to understand why the advective family saturates toward a bounded plateau at fixed release rate.

cases.display_name: ECHA bounded-clearance edge case family
summary_lines: This governed reference case family anchors screening claims about bounded concentration under effective persistence when a finite residence-time loss term remains present.
It is intended to ground weak-clearance versus strong-clearance reviewer challenges in regulator-recognizable environmental assessment concepts.
applicability_lines: Appropriate for extreme-persistence or residence-time edge claims in the advective screening family.
Not a claim of full multimedia EUSES equivalence or a substitute for site-specific water-body characterization.

source_references.title: ECHA Guidance on Information Requirements and Chemical Safety Assessment
ECHA EUSES support page

review_notes: Use this case family to explain why bounded clearance still matters under effective persistence in one-compartment flowing-water screening.

cases.display_name: ECHA elapsed-time flowing-water screening case family
summary_lines: This governed reference case family anchors elapsed-time bucket behavior for one-compartment flowing-water screening to regulator-recognizable EU environmental assessment concepts.
It supports reviewer-facing discussion of why advective time-bucket outputs preserve elapsed physical time and post-release decline rather than arbitrary pagination.
applicability_lines: Appropriate for EU-grounded explanation of elapsed-time semantics in bounded flowing-water screening outputs.
Not a substitute for routed hydrologic or hydrodynamic time-series modelling.

source_references.title: ECHA Guidance on Information Requirements and Chemical Safety Assessment

cases.display_name: ECHA EUSES water screening case family
summary_lines: This governed reference case family anchors one-compartment flowing-water screening interpretations against regulator-recognizable EUSES-style environmental exposure concepts.
It is used as a screening reference family for residence-time and bounded-clearance reasoning, not as a claim that Fate MCP implements EUSES directly.
applicability_lines: Appropriate for reviewer-facing mapping of flowing-water screening concepts where bounded clearance and compartment residence time are material.
Not a substitute for full multimedia EUSES implementation or dossier-specific environmental exposure modelling.

cases.display_name: ECHA post-release flushing boundary case family

applicability_lines: Appropriate for post-release turnover-boundary and recovery-interpretation claims in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for routed hydrodynamic recovery modelling, site observations, or full EUSES implementation.

cases.display_name: EPA post-release recovery directionality case family

applicability_lines: Appropriate for post-release directionality claims that need explicit sub-boundary, boundary, and beyond-boundary recovery interpretation in the advective screening family.
Not a substitute for routed receiving-water recovery modelling, monitoring data, or calibrated hydrodynamic post-release analysis.
